board.title: Sounds
board.reconnect: Reconnect Twitch once so darkbot gets its new permissions: creating rewards and reading chat for song requests.
board.onboardText: darkbot listens for channel point redemptions and plays the sound you assign to each reward.
board.emptyText: Assign a sound to one of your channel point rewards.
board.hint: Click a pad to preview it. Viewers trigger it with channel points.
feed.title: Activity
feed.empty: Redemptions, follows and other channel events appear here. darkbot keeps them across restarts.
feed.queueFull: Too many sounds waiting, not played
settings.title: Settings
general.title: General
general.languageHint: Changes the app right away. The log stays in English so it can be shared in bug reports.
audio.title: Where sounds play
audio.modeDeviceText: darkbot plays the sound on the output you pick. Capture it in OBS.
audio.modeObsText: darkbot plays the sound in an OBS media source on the tracks you pick.
audio.hintChoose: To get it into OBS, pick a virtual cable or spare output and add it as Audio Output Capture. Or keep the default and add darkbot itself with Application Audio Capture.
audio.hintNoChoose: This system doesn’t let darkbot list outputs, so sounds play on the system default. In OBS add darkbot with Application Audio Capture (Windows) or macOS Audio Capture, or choose “Inside OBS”.
audio.tracksHint: Same tracks as in OBS Advanced Audio Properties. Track 1 is usually the stream.
audio.inputHint: Created in the current scene when missing. OBS only plays sources in the active scene, so add it to your other scenes as an existing source.
audio.savedObsOffline: Audio output saved. Connect OBS in the OBS section to play sounds there.
twitch.title: Twitch
twitch.statusOff: Not connected. Connect to let viewers play sounds with channel points.
twitch.statusReconnect: Connected as {login}. Disconnect and connect again so darkbot gets its new permissions (rewards, chat).
twitch.affiliateHint: Channel points need an Affiliate or Partner channel.
obs.title: OBS connection
obs.lede: Needed for “Inside OBS”. In OBS open Tools, then WebSocket Server Settings, and enable the server.
obs.passwordKeep: Leave empty to keep the saved one
obs.auto: Connect automatically, also when OBS starts later
obs.authFailed: OBS rejected the password. Copy it from OBS (Tools, WebSocket Server Settings, Show Connect Info) and connect again.
obs.waiting: Waiting for OBS… darkbot connects as soon as OBS runs.
updates.title: Updates
updates.dev: Development build. Builds made on this computer don’t update themselves.
updates.auto: Install updates automatically when darkbot starts
updates.autoHint: While darkbot is running, new versions are only announced, so a stream is never interrupted.
log.title: Log
editor.newHint: darkbot creates this reward on your channel and keeps it in sync. If a sound can’t play, the redemption is rejected so the viewer gets the points back.
editor.existingHint: darkbot only listens to rewards it didn’t create. It can’t change them or give points back.
editor.noRewards: Your channel has no custom rewards yet.
editor.cooldownHint: Nobody can trigger it again during this time.
editor.userCooldownHint: The same viewer has to wait this long.
editor.deleteConfirmReward: Click again, this also deletes the reward on Twitch
play.cannotPlay: the app window could not play this file
play.noSink: choosing an output device is not supported on this system
err.updateRunning: an update is already being installed
err.noClientID: this darkbot build has no Twitch Client ID (see README, Build from source)
err.pathAbsolute: the sound file path must be absolute
err.rewardName: the reward name must be 1 to {max} characters
err.rewardColor: the color must be a hex color like #9147FF
err.price: the price must be between {min} and {max} points
err.reconnect: reconnect Twitch so darkbot may create rewards (Settings, Twitch, Disconnect, Connect)
err.noPlaybackConfirm: no playback confirmation from the app window after {seconds} s
err.tokenRejected: Twitch rejected the login, please connect again
err.notAffiliate: channel points need a Twitch Affiliate or Partner account
err.notOwner: this reward was created outside darkbot, so darkbot can’t change it
err.obsAuth: OBS rejected the password: copy it from OBS (Tools → WebSocket Server Settings → Show Connect Info)
err.obsConnect: OBS is not reachable at {addr} (is OBS running and Tools → WebSocket Server Settings enabled?)
chat.usage: Use !sr followed by a song link or a song name.
chat.offline: Song requests aren’t available right now.
chat.cooldown: Please wait {seconds} s before your next request.
chat.error: Something went wrong, please try again later.
chat.unavailable: This song can’t be played here.
chat.tooLong: Songs can be at most {minutes} minutes long.
err.spotifyRejected: Spotify rejected the login, please connect Spotify again
err.spotifyClientID: enter your Spotify Client ID first
err.spotifyPasteEmpty: paste the address from your browser
err.spotifyPasteInvalid: that doesn’t look like the address Spotify sent you to
err.spotifyPasteOld: this address belongs to an older login attempt, please start again
err.spotifyNoDevice: Spotify isn’t playing on any device, start playback in Spotify first
err.spotifyPremium: the Spotify queue needs Spotify Premium
err.spotifyRateLimit: Spotify is busy, please try again in a moment
err.spotifyNotTrack: only links to single songs work, not albums or playlists
err.spotifyLinkType: this kind of Spotify link isn’t supported, use the song’s share link
songs.title: Song requests
songs.lede: Viewers add songs from chat to your queue on Spotify, YouTube Music or both. A song link goes to the service it belongs to; a song name is searched where you choose below.
songs.chatMissing: Reconnect Twitch once (Settings, Twitch) so darkbot can read and answer chat.
songs.step1: Open the Spotify developer dashboard and log in with the Spotify account you stream with. Create an app; name and description can be anything.
songs.step2: Under Redirect URIs add exactly this address:
songs.step3: Under the APIs to use, tick Web API, accept the terms and save.
songs.step4: Open the app’s settings, copy the Client ID and paste it below. A Spotify app serves at most 5 users, which is why every streamer creates their own.
songs.copyFailed: Couldn’t copy. Select the address and copy it yourself.
songs.pasteHelp: Allow access in the browser. Afterwards the browser shows an error page like “This site can’t be reached”. That’s expected, because darkbot opens no port. Copy the whole address from the address bar and paste it here.
songs.enabled: Song requests in chat are on
songs.cooldownHint: How long a viewer waits between two requests. You and your moderators have no wait.
songs.requesterSkip: Viewers may skip the song they requested
songs.cmdSr: Adds a song: a Spotify or YouTube Music song link, or a name, for example !sr bohemian rhapsody
songs.cmdSkip: Skips the current song: you, your moderators and, if allowed above, whoever requested it
songs.legal: Playing music you hold no rights to can get your VODs muted or your channel a DMCA strike on Twitch, and the terms of Spotify and YouTube don’t allow broadcasting. What you play is your call.
chat.alreadyQueued: This song is already playing or in the queue.
credit.title: Opens tarkov-stammtisch.de in your browser
tip.sigTwitch: Your Twitch login. Lit means darkbot is logged in to your channel. Grey: open Settings, Twitch and connect.
tip.sigEvents: The live line to Twitch that delivers channel point redemptions (and chat commands). Lit means redemptions arrive right now. If it stays grey, check your internet or reconnect Twitch.
tip.sigObs: Connection to OBS. Only needed when sounds play “Inside OBS”.
tip.master: Volume for all sounds at once. Each sound also has its own volume; both are multiplied. Song requests aren’t affected, Spotify has its own volume.
tip.language: The language of the app and of darkbot’s answers in your chat. “Same as system” follows your computer’s language.
tip.modeDevice: darkbot plays sounds itself, like a media player. Simple and works without OBS. In OBS you capture the sound with an audio capture source, so it’s on stream.
tip.modeObs: darkbot tells OBS to play the sound in its own media source. You then choose exactly which OBS audio tracks get it, for example stream yes, VOD no. Needs the OBS connection.
tip.device: Which speaker or virtual cable the sounds go to. A virtual cable (e.g. VB-Cable, VoiceMeeter) keeps sounds off your headphones but on stream when you capture it in OBS.
tip.tracks: OBS can record up to 6 separate audio tracks. Track 1 is usually what viewers hear live. Leave a track off, for example your VOD track, to keep sounds out of it.
tip.inputName: The name of the media source darkbot uses in OBS. darkbot creates it if it’s missing. Only rename it if the name clashes with one of your sources.
tip.obsHost: Where OBS runs. “localhost” means this computer. With a second streaming PC, enter that PC’s IP address.
tip.obsPort: The port of the OBS WebSocket server, shown in OBS under Tools, WebSocket Server Settings. Default is 4455.
tip.obsPassword: The server password from OBS (Tools, WebSocket Server Settings, Show Connect Info). darkbot stores it on this computer only and never shows it again.
tip.obsAuto: darkbot connects when it starts and reconnects by itself whenever OBS is (re)started, also if OBS was closed in between. Without this, you connect by hand once; darkbot then also reconnects until you click Disconnect.
tip.autoUpdate: When on, darkbot installs a new version right when it starts, before you go live. During a stream it never updates by itself.
tip.redirect: Spotify only sends logins back to addresses you registered. Copy this one exactly into your Spotify app. Nothing runs at this address; the error page you’ll see is expected.
tip.spotifyClientId: The ID of YOUR Spotify app from the developer dashboard, a long string of letters and digits. Not your Spotify password, and you never need the Client Secret.
tip.spotifyPaste: After you allowed access, the browser tries to open 127.0.0.1 and shows an error. Click into the address bar, copy everything (it contains “code=”) and paste it here.
tip.songsEnabled: Master switch for !sr, !song, !next, !queue and !skip. Off means darkbot ignores these commands completely.
tip.songsCooldown: How many seconds a viewer must wait between two song requests. Stops one person from filling your queue. 0 = no wait.
tip.songsMax: Songs longer than this are refused, so nobody queues a one-hour mix. 0 = any length.
tip.songsExplicit: Refuses songs marked “E” (explicit lyrics) on Spotify or YouTube Music. Not every song is marked, so this is a filter, not a guarantee.
tip.songsRequesterSkip: When on, the viewer who requested the song playing right now can skip it with !skip. You and your moderators can always skip.
tip.songsReplies: darkbot answers commands in your chat, e.g. “Added to the queue”. The answers are sent from your own Twitch account.
tip.rewardName: The name viewers see on the channel point reward. Max. 45 characters. Changing it here also renames it on Twitch.
tip.price: How many channel points viewers pay. Viewers collect points by watching; 100–1,000 is a common range for sounds.
tip.rewardColor: The background color of the reward on Twitch, so viewers find it quickly. Click the color field for the color picker, type a hex code like #9147FF, or take a suggestion.
tip.existingReward: A reward you created on Twitch yourself. darkbot plays the sound when it’s redeemed, but can’t change the reward or refund points; that’s Twitch’s rule for rewards from other apps.
tip.file: The audio file that plays. darkbot reads it from this place on your computer, so don’t move or delete it afterwards.
tip.volume: Volume of this one sound, to even out loud and quiet files. Combined with the master volume at the bottom.
tip.cooldown: After the sound played, nobody can trigger it for this many seconds. For rewards darkbot created, Twitch also blocks the reward meanwhile and shows viewers the countdown from 60 s on.
tip.userCooldown: How long the same viewer has to wait before triggering this sound again. If they redeem too early, the sound doesn’t play; for rewards darkbot created, Twitch also gives the points back.
tip.enabled: Off pauses the sound without deleting it. For rewards darkbot created, the reward is also hidden on Twitch.
dash.title: Dashboard
dash.resetTitle: Sets this session’s counters to zero, e.g. when a new stream starts. Totals stay.
dash.resetConfirm: Click again to start a new session
dash.topViewersEmpty: Nobody yet. Viewers appear here when they redeem sounds or request songs.
tip.dashRedemptions: Every channel point redemption of one of your sound rewards this session. Played = ran to the end. Refused = didn’t play (cooldown, sound off, queue full or error). Your own previews aren’t counted.
tip.dashCommands: Song request commands from chat that darkbot handled: !sr, !song, !next, !queue and !skip. Repeats by the same viewer within 3 seconds are ignored and not counted.
tip.dashSongs: Songs that went into your Spotify queue with !sr. Refused = not found, too long, explicit, already queued or a Spotify problem.
tip.dashViewers: How many different viewers redeemed a sound or got a song into the queue this session.
logins.title: Logins
logins.expired: expired, renewed the next time it’s needed
logins.autoOnUse: the next time Spotify is used
tip.logins: darkbot keeps your logins alive by itself. The short-lived access is renewed before it runs out, so you never have to log in again during a stream. “Renew now” does it immediately, for example to test it.
general.autostart: Start darkbot when I log in to my computer
general.autostartOn: darkbot now starts when you log in.
tip.closeToTray: On: the X button hides darkbot to the notification area next to the clock, and sounds, chat and events keep working. Click the icon to open it again, quit it from its menu (right click). Off: the X button quits darkbot.
general.closeToTray: Closing the window keeps darkbot running in the tray
tip.autostart: Adds darkbot to the system start: Windows autostart (starts quietly in the tray), macOS login items or Linux autostart. Only for your user account, no admin rights needed. Updates keep working.
eventdesc.unfollow: Someone stopped following. Only with unfollow detection on; Twitch itself never reports this.
eventdesc.sub: Someone subscribes with their own money. Gifted subs run "Gifted subs" instead.
eventdesc.resub: A subscriber shares their resub in chat.
eventdesc.gift: A viewer gifts one or more subs (a sub bomb): runs once per gift, the number is how many. Recipients don’t trigger anything extra.
eventdesc.raid: Another streamer raids you with their viewers.
eventdesc.hype_begin: Your chat started a hype train.
eventdesc.hype_level: The hype train reaches a new level; the number is the new level. "From" sets the lowest level that runs the action.
eventdesc.hype_end: The hype train is over; the number is the level reached, {top} is whoever contributed most.
eventdesc.shoutout: Another streamer gave you a shoutout.
eventdesc.ad_break: An ad break starts on your channel.
eventdesc.sub_end: A subscription ended (not renewed or a gift ran out).
eventdesc.online: Your stream went live. The dashboard starts a new session by itself.
events.title: Events
events.lede: Everything that happens on your channel appears in the activity feed. Here you choose what darkbot does on top: play a sound, write in chat, or both.
events.reconnect: Reconnect Twitch once so darkbot may receive follows, subs, Bits, hype trains, ads and shoutouts.
events.tested: Test sent: watch the feed, and the chat if a message is set.
events.unfollowOff: Off. Twitch has no unfollow event, so darkbot would compare your follower list every 10 minutes.
events.unfollowTooMany: Not possible: your channel has {n} followers, the limit is 5,000.
tip.unfollow: Twitch tells nobody about unfollows. So darkbot reads your follower list every 10 minutes and reports who is missing. Unfollows can show up to 10 minutes late, and deleted or banned accounts count too. darkbot keeps the list, so on the next start it also finds follows and unfollows from while it was off (marked “while off”, no sound). Up to 5,000 followers; unfollows never get a chat message.
evedit.chatHint: Placeholders: {user} name, {amount} amount (Bits, viewers, subs, level, streams of a watch streak), {tier} sub tier, {months} months, {top} biggest hype train contributor, {points} channel points for a watch streak. Sent from your account. Leave empty for no message.
evdefault.sub: Thanks for subscribing, {user}! Welcome to the crew!
evdefault.resub: {user} has been here for {months} months, thank you for sticking around!
evdefault.gift: {user} just gifted {amount} subs, thank you so much!
evdefault.raid: Welcome, raiders! Thanks {user} for the raid with {amount} viewers!
evdefault.hype_begin: The hype train is rolling, all aboard!
evdefault.hype_level: Hype train level {amount}! Keep it going!
evdefault.hype_end: Hype train over at level {amount}! Thanks everyone, especially {top}!
evdefault.ad_break: Short ad break ({amount} seconds), we’ll be right back!
evdefault.offline: Thanks for watching, see you next time!
tip.evAlert: Shows a picture, GIF or video and/or a text in OBS while the event’s sound plays. Needs the OBS connection and the darkbot scene (Settings, OBS).
tip.evOverlayText: Shown under the picture in OBS. Same placeholders as the chat message. Change font and colour on the source "[darkbot] text" in OBS.
tip.evSeconds: How long the alert stays. 0 = automatic: the video’s length, or 5 seconds for a picture. The sound always plays to the end.
evedit.alertNoObs: OBS is not connected: the alert is skipped until it is.
evedit.alertNoScene: The darkbot scene is not in all your OBS scenes yet: set it up in Settings, OBS.
evedit.alertReady: Ready: OBS is connected and the darkbot scene is in all your scenes.
tip.obsScene: darkbot keeps everything it shows or plays in its own scene "[darkbot]" and adds that scene on top of each of your scenes. Nothing else in your scenes is changed. Move or restyle the alert sources inside the [darkbot] scene as you like. "Remove from OBS" takes it all out again.
obs.sceneMissing: The darkbot scene doesn’t exist yet. One click creates it and adds it to all your scenes.
obs.sceneMissingIn: The darkbot scene is missing in: {scenes}
obs.sceneReady: The darkbot scene is in all {n} of your scenes.
obs.setupAdded: Added the darkbot scene to {n} scenes.
dialog.chooseVisual: Choose a picture, GIF or video
err.visualType: use a picture or video file ({types})
err.overlayTooLong: the text on screen may have at most {max} characters
err.alertSeconds: the alert can stay 0 to {max} seconds
tip.evSuggest: Puts darkbot’s suggested message for this event into the field. Change it as you like; nothing is sent until you save and switch the action on.
evedit.minHint: Smaller amounts still appear in the feed, just without the action. 0 = always.
tip.evSound: Plays through the same output and queue as your channel point sounds, so nothing talks over each other.
tip.evChat: darkbot writes this into your chat when the event happens. What viewers typed (cheer or resub messages) is never copied, so nobody can make darkbot post their text.
tip.evMin: For Bits the number of Bits, for raids the number of viewers, for gifts the number of subs, for watch streaks the streams in a row.
tip.dashFollows: Big number: new follows this session. Below: your follower count as Twitch shows it now (updated every 5 minutes and after each follow). Unfollows only count with unfollow detection on (Events).
tip.dashSubs: Big number: new subs and resubs this session; gifted subs are counted separately, once per gift. Below: your active subs and sub points as Twitch counts them now (points unlock emote slots: tier 1 = 1, tier 2 = 2, tier 3 = 6).
tip.dashBits: All Bits cheered in your chat this session. Twitch offers no all-time Bits total, so "Total" is what darkbot counted.
tip.dashRaids: Incoming raids this session and how many viewers they brought. Twitch offers no raid history, so "Total" is what darkbot counted.
err.chatTooLong: the chat message can be at most {max} characters
obs.removed: darkbot is removed from OBS: the [darkbot] scene, its sources and every place it was added to.
cmds.title: Chat
cmds.lede: Your own commands like !discord, and timers that post in your chat regularly. darkbot writes with your Twitch account. Both stay off until you turn them on.
cmds.missing: Reconnect Twitch once (Settings, Twitch) so darkbot may read and write your chat.
tip.commandsOn: Main switch for all commands below. Off means darkbot answers none of them. The song commands (!sr etc.) are under Settings, Song requests.
cmds.noCommands: No commands yet. Add, for example, !discord with your invite link.
tip.timersOn: Main switch for all timers below. Timers post only while you are live. After the stream starts each timer first waits its whole interval.
cmds.noTimers: No timers yet. A timer posts, for example, "Follow for more!" every 20 minutes.
cmds.timersLive: You are live: timers are running.
cmds.timersWaiting: Timers wait until you go live.
cmdedit.name: Command
tip.cmdName: What viewers type after the !. Letters, digits and _, no spaces. Upper and lower case don't matter.
tip.cmdAliases: Other names for the same command, separated by commas, e.g. dc for !discord.
tip.cmdResponse: What darkbot writes in chat. Leave it empty if the command should only play a sound.
cmdedit.responseHint: Placeholders: {user} is who typed the command, {target} the name after it (e.g. !hug @Anna), otherwise {user} again. Other viewer text is never used.
tip.cmdCooldown: After a use the command waits this long for everyone, or per viewer. You yourself can always use it.
tip.cmdSound: Plays when the command is used. It runs in the same queue as all sounds, never at the same time as another.
timeredit.messagePlaceholder: Enjoying the stream? Follow so you don't miss the next one!
tip.timerInterval: How often the message comes, at least every 5 minutes. When several timers are due together they come one minute apart.
tip.timerLines: This many chat messages must have come since the last post, so darkbot never writes into an empty chat. 0 means any.
err.cmdName: "{name}" can't be a command: only letters, digits and _, no spaces, at most 25 characters
err.cmdEmpty: enter an answer or choose a sound
err.cmdPermission: choose who may use the command
err.cmdCooldown: the cooldown can be 0 to {max} seconds
err.timerInterval: a timer can come every {min} to {max} minutes
eventdesc.watch_streak: A viewer shares in chat how many streams in a row they watched.
feed.ev.watch_streak: {user} shares a watch streak of {amount} streams
evdefault.watch_streak: Wow {user}, {amount} streams in a row! Thanks for sticking around!
feed.clearTitle: Removes every line from the activity list. darkbot keeps the last 200 lines, also across restarts and updates.
feed.missedTitle: Happened while darkbot was not running; found when it compared the follower list. No sound or chat message was sent.
chat.busy: Too many song requests right now, please try again in a minute.
err.soundTooBig: The sound file is larger than {mb} MB. Use a shorter or compressed file (MP3, OGG).
chat.addedNoTitle: Added your song to the queue.
chat.titlesHidden: Song titles aren’t posted in chat here.
tip.songsTitles: darkbot names the song in its answers, e.g. “Added to the queue: Artist – Title”. Titles on Spotify and YouTube can be any text and are posted from your own account, which AutoMod doesn’t filter. Turn this off and darkbot answers without titles; !song, !next and !queue then only say that titles aren’t posted.
chat.linkUnsupported: This kind of link doesn’t work here. Use a song link or the song’s name.
chat.serviceOff: {service} songs don’t work here right now.
err.ytmNotRunning: Pear Desktop isn’t reachable: start it and turn on its API Server plugin
err.ytmNotAuthorized: Pear Desktop no longer accepts darkbot, connect YouTube Music again
err.ytmDenied: access was denied in Pear Desktop
err.ytmNotSongLink: only links to single songs work, not playlists or channels
err.ytmNotAdded: YouTube Music didn’t take the song
err.ytmBusy: darkbot is already waiting for Pear Desktop
err.ytmTimeout: Pear Desktop didn’t answer in time. Click Allow in its window and try again
songs.ytmLede: Works through Pear Desktop, the free open-source YouTube Music app for Windows, macOS and Linux. Pear Desktop has to be running while you stream.
songs.ytmStep1: Install Pear Desktop and sign in to YouTube Music there.
songs.ytmStep2: In Pear Desktop open the Plugins menu and turn on “API Server [Beta]”.
songs.ytmStep3: In the same plugin menu set Hostname to 127.0.0.1, so only this computer can reach it. Leave HTTPS off and the authorization strategy at “Authorize at first request”.
songs.ytmStep4: Click Connect below, then Allow in the window Pear Desktop shows.
songs.ytmWaiting: Waiting for you to click Allow in Pear Desktop…
tip.ytmPort: The port in Pear Desktop’s API Server menu. Change it here only if you changed it there. Pear Desktop’s default is 26538.
tip.searchService: !sr with a link always goes to the service the link belongs to. !sr with a song name searches here. If this service isn’t connected, darkbot searches on the other one.
